text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Reports by Radio Zambia and the Zambian News Agency allege that there is a move to campaign for the secession of Zambia's western region Barotseland to become part of Namibia. The Namibian Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it had no knowledge of an alleged plot, but the reports would be investigated.

- The number of projects by the National Housing Enterprise dropped by 62 percent last last compared to 1995 due to higher interest rates and lack of funds. The parastatal which aims to provide cheap housing built only 155 homes in 1996.
- Southern Namibia has received the best rains in many years. There is water in the famous Sossusvlei in the Namib desert for the first time since 1990.
- The University of Namibia has appealed to the public to rent our rooms and flats because over 3,000 students need accommodation.
